title: cli: `os secret rewrap --apply` in a non-interactive shell without `--yes` prints "Aborted" and exits 0 — the confirmation family (migrate, orphans --delete) exits 1
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-alice · session_011y7As7qKGpBTzxc5S8q3Ko

Filing gate: ① out-of-scope finding, class a · Source: fleet · the os-dev report on PR #36676 (#36331), `out_of_scope_findings`. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

`os secret rewrap --apply`, run without `--yes` where stdin is not a terminal (a script, CI, a cron job), prints `Aborted — no row was opened or written.` and returns exit 0. A script reads success; nothing was re-sealed.

Read from source on origin/main 3cf6a44b (reach not measured at a running deployment):

- `packages/cli/src/commands/secret/rewrap.ts:353-361` — `if (flags.apply && plan.attempts > 0 && !flags.yes)`: the `--json` face emits `confirmation_required` and exits 1; the text face calls the shared `confirm(...)`, which answers `false` when stdin is not a TTY, then `printInfo('Aborted — …'); return;` (exit 0).

## Why it is a defect

The family rule: a run that did not get its confirmation applies nothing and exits 1, naming `--yes` (#24949, `packages/cli/test/migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts`). #36331 / PR #36676 brings `os db orphans --delete` and `os secret orphans --delete` under it with a sibling pin, `packages/cli/test/orphans-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts`, whose population is commands declaring boolean `delete` and `yes` flags. `secret rewrap` gates on `--apply`, not `--delete`, so neither pin's population reaches it.

## Done when

- `os secret rewrap --apply`, text face, non-TTY, no `--yes`: exit 1 with a line naming `--yes`; nothing opened or written (as today).
- An interactive "no" stays as the family treats it (exit 0 in the migrate and orphans pins' controls).
- The pin population covers apply-behind-`--yes` modes outside `src/commands/migrate/**` (widen the orphans pin's population, or a sibling pin), with an ablation, so the next command of this shape is caught by construction.

Out of scope: what rewrap opens, re-seals or writes.

reach: read from source only, same shape as #36331 (measured there by its dev on the sibling commands).
Business reason: an operator's scripted key rotation reads as done while no secret was re-sealed.
Dedupe: `rewrap in:title,body` 16 hits, `rewrap Aborted` 7 hits, `"--yes" exit 0 non-interactive` 16 hits (all states) — none names the rewrap text face; nearest are #36331 (open, sibling commands) and #24949 (closed, the rule).
Suggested-grade: p2 · same class and reach as #36331, which triage graded p2.
